quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey instructions from flaggers. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic light.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against the light. Pedestrians may misjudge traffic signals.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum and minimum speeds allowed on that road. The maximum is for good conditions. You must drive slower when weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair your judgment and coordination. This can happen at any BAC level, even below the legal limit. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights in fog. High beams point upward and bounce off fog, reducing visibility. Low beams work better.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is coming. You should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
Keep steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Then safely pass the pedestrian.

questions.question: Following a motorcycle too closely is dangerous because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as cars.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than most cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than most cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than cars. Following too closely is dangerous. You need time and space to avoid a crash if the motorcycle suddenly stops.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. You:

options.text: Have done as much as you can.
Must wait for police to arrive.
Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say no to a drink if someone offers you one and you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving risks is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions after you have started drinking.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you drive too fast, your tires lose their grip and slide on a film of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what will most likely happen?

options.text: You will interfere with traffic and may get a ticket.
You will be using good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will interfere with traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You should drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you block normal traffic flow by driving too slowly, you may get a ticket. You should match the speed of traffic unless traffic is speeding above the legal limit.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what will happen next?
questions.correctAnswerText: A steady red light
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear soon.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
In all of the above situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all of the above situations.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because it is unlikely another vehicle is coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the highway shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic blocks the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if vehicles are blocking your path. If you are in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip wet, snowy, or icy roads as well as dry roads. You should reduce your speed in these conditions.

questions.question: If you keep a valid license for one full year without getting moving violations, you may earn a Good Point on your record.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: If you maintain a valid driver's license for a full calendar year without any moving violations, you may be eligible to earn a Good Point on your driving record.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop at a yield sign, but you can continue without stopping if there is no other traffic.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to possible dangers. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet, making it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely and easily. This helps both drivers avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that an intersection is ahead. A road will join from the right side.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children must be secured in proper child seats or safety belts. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use proper safety seats for children.
